from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Vectors are arrows in 2D space.", "Scaling changes vector magnitude.", "Adding vectors shifts positions."]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Intuition: The Vector Space", lecture_lines)
        
        # Assets
        v_color = "#FF5733"
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Create 2D vector 'v' in color #FF5733 appearing from origin.
        v_arrow = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*2 + UP*1, color=v_color, buff=0)
        v_label = MathTex("v", color=v_color).next_to(v_arrow.get_end(), UP+RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        # Place the vector system in the right grid area
        vector_group = VGroup(v_arrow, v_label)
        self.place_in_area(vector_group, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Create(v_arrow), Write(v_label))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(v_color)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show scalar multiplication 2*v
        v_double = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=(RIGHT*2 + UP*1)*2, color="#33FF57", buff=0)
        label_double = MathTex("2v", color="#33FF57").next_to(v_double.get_end(), UP+RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.place_in_area(VGroup(v_double, label_double), 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Transform(v_arrow, v_double), Transform(v_label, label_double))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#33FF57")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Adding vectors
        v2 = Arrow(start=v_arrow.get_end(), end=v_arrow.get_end() + LEFT*1 + UP*2, color="#5733FF", buff=0)
        v_sum = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=v_arrow.get_end() + v2.get_end() - v_arrow.get_end(), color="#FFFF33", buff=0)
        
        self.play(Create(v2), Create(v_sum))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF33")
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Linear Dependence: Redundancy", ["Dependence reveals redundant directions.", "A third vector adds no reach.", "Like hikers following one trail."])
        
        # Setup vectors
        u = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*1.5, color=BLUE).shift(self.grid["D2"])
        v = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=UP*1.5, color=GREEN).shift(self.grid["D2"])
        w = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=(RIGHT+UP)*1.5, color=RED).shift(self.grid["D2"])
        
        u_label = MathTex("u", color=BLUE).next_to(u.get_end(), RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        v_label = MathTex("v", color=GREEN).next_to(v.get_end(), UP, buff=0.1)
        w_label = MathTex("w=u+v", color=RED).next_to(w.get_end(), UP+RIGHT, buff=0.1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Create(u), Write(u_label), Create(v), Write(v_label), Create(w), Write(w_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(FadeOut(w), FadeOut(w_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Indicate(u), Indicate(v))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Basis is the minimal span set.", "It removes all redundant vectors.", "Basis acts as coordinate frames."]
        self.setup_layout("Basis: The Minimalist Framework", lecture_lines)
        
        # Setup Axes
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.5)
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'B2', 'E5')

        i_vec = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=axes.c2p(1, 0), color="#FF33FF", buff=0)
        j_vec = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=axes.c2p(0, 1), color="#33FFFF", buff=0)
        v_vec = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=axes.c2p(1.5, 2), color=YELLOW, buff=0)
        
        i_label = MathTex(r"\vec{i}", color="#FF33FF").next_to(i_vec.get_end(), DOWN)
        j_label = MathTex(r"\vec{j}", color="#33FFFF").next_to(j_vec.get_end(), LEFT)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF33FF"))
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(i_vec), Create(j_vec), Write(i_label), Write(j_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#33FFFF"))
        # Indicate redundancy - visually clear
        redundant_vec = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=axes.c2p(0.5, 0.5), color=GRAY, buff=0)
        self.play(Create(redundant_vec))
        self.play(FadeOut(redundant_vec))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Create(v_vec))
        grid = NumberPlane(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3]).scale(0.5)
        self.place_in_area(grid, 'B2', 'E5')
        self.play(FadeIn(grid), run_time=2)
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis and Summary", [
            "Span defines your total reach.", 
            "Dependence marks redundant paths.", 
            "Basis builds the perfect frame."
        ])
        
        # Setup visualization objects
        triangle = Polygon(ORIGIN, RIGHT*2 + UP*1.5, RIGHT*4, color=WHITE)
        span_dot = Dot(triangle.get_vertices()[0], color=BLUE)
        dep_dot = Dot(triangle.get_vertices()[1], color=RED)
        basis_dot = Dot(triangle.get_vertices()[2], color=GREEN)
        
        frame = VGroup(triangle, span_dot, dep_dot, basis_dot)
        self.place_in_area(frame, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.8)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Create(frame), run_time=1)
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(Indicate(dep_dot), run_time=1)
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(RED))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(Indicate(basis_dot), run_time=1)
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.play(FadeOut(frame), run_time=1)

outline.topic: Foundations of Linear Algebra: From Span to Basis

sections.title: Prerequisite Intuition: The Vector Space
sections.content: Briefly define a vector as an arrow in 2D space. Introduce the concept of 'scaling' and 'adding' vectors as geometric movements (tip-to-tail).
sections.example: A robotic arm moving 2 units East and 3 units North.

sections.title: Linear Combinations and Span
sections.content: Explain that a linear combination is the result of scaling vectors and adding them together. 'Span' is the set of all possible destinations reachable by varying these scale factors.
sections.example: Visualizing two vectors as 'basis' directions: combining them covers the entire 2D plane like a grid.

sections.title: Linear Dependence: Redundancy
sections.content: Introduce linear dependence visually: when a third vector lies on the same line or plane as the others, it adds no new 'reach.' It's redundant information.
sections.example: Three hikers: If hiker A and B are walking on the same trail, hiker C (who is just following them) is linearly dependent.

sections.title: Basis: The Minimalist Framework
sections.content: Define 'Basis' as the smallest set of vectors that span the entire space without any redundancy (linearly independent). This is the 'minimal coordinate system' for the space.
sections.example: Using standard basis vectors (1,0) and (0,1) to describe the location of a pixel on a digital screen.

sections.title: Synthesis and Summary
sections.content: Wrap up: Span defines the 'reach,' Linear Dependence checks for 'redundancy,' and Basis provides the 'perfect frame.'
sections.example: A GPS system needing exactly 3 satellites (a basis) to pinpoint a coordinate in 3D space.
